subfamily: sour: a Whiskey Sour (Regan, Joy pdf 406: bourbon or rye, lemon, simple syrup), sweetened instead with granulated sugar muddled with the squeezed lemon shell, as Regan advises for a Whiskey Sour (Joy pdf 151: 'the sugar abrades the zest of the lemons and produces a far fresher-tasting drink'); lemon cut from his 30 ml to 20 ml for acid
glass: small stemmed sour glass (about 180 ml), chilled in the freezer, no ice

ingredients.note: squeezed from half a medium lemon and measured; the squeezed shell, cut in four, is muddled with the sugar for its zest and gives up a few drops more (swept to 22.5 ml)
granulated white sugar, 2 1/2 teaspoons, muddled with the lemon shell and juice

_status: v1 (Tomás, round 2). Rejected on paper: Regan's printed 60/30/15 simple (acid OUT 1.11 vs 0.76-0.94); 60/30 with 8-16 g sugar (acid OUT 1.15-1.21 at every sugar); 60/25 (acid OUT 1.03); bottled-in-bond 50% (strength OUT 21.1-21.5). 60/20/11 g all in at 40% and 45%; shell yield to +2.5 ml only edges acid (0.95).
